visualization.name: RustGIS
visualization.description: Explore geographic data and LAS/LAZ point clouds with RustGIS
visualization.help:
# RustGIS
Explore geographic data using the RustGIS browser application: maps, styling, attribute tables, editing, layouts and browser-supported spatial analysis. Save and Export download files to your computer; edits are not automatically saved to Galaxy history.
Supported inputs: GeoJSON, LAS/LAZ, CSV/TSV with coordinate or WKT columns, georeferenced TIFF, GeoParquet, and ZIP archives of Shapefiles or other supported vector data. A Galaxy composite Shapefile must first be packaged as a ZIP. Plain Parquet without supported geospatial metadata is not supported.
Deferred HTTP(S) datasets load directly from their source, leaving the Galaxy dataset deferred. The external server must allow browser requests from your Galaxy origin (CORS) and provide appropriate access. Sources requiring Galaxy file-source credentials or transformations must first be materialized. HTTPS Galaxy pages require HTTPS sources.
LAS/LAZ are displayed as sampled point layers, including elevation, classification, intensity and available RGB. At most 500,000 points are displayed; LAZ sampling considers up to the first 40 million points. Remote LAZ and COPC files download completely, with a 256 MiB browser download limit. COPC spatial streaming is not available. Use smaller extracts for large clouds.
WebGPU or WebGL2 and WebAssembly are required. Native GDAL/DuckDB features and direct database connections are unavailable. Read more at https://github.com/opengeos/RustGIS.
